Evidence: Merged in cf5465b85 (redoubt). tests/unsafe-budget.toml lists every on-target source: kernel core 25, arch 13, backends 16, redoubt-wire 0, redoubt-abi 52 (44 undocumented, recorded as K6 legacy debt in SWARM Review debt); ceilings equal the counted existing uses. ### G1 clear review debt — implementer · Question

Event: `441517a8df43ba9792ac6d4db388d234` · 2026-09-24T05:35:10Z

> G1 finding. What should happen to unsafe code that no budget counts? This is the unsafe ratchet's coverage inventory, not a checker bug.
> 
> Evidence (HEAD adcfda055): `cargo testbench unsafe-budget` exits 0 and every configured root is counted honestly. I ran a scan using the checker's own counting rule (tools/testbench/src/budget.rs count_file) on every tracked .rs file outside the configured roots in tests/unsafe-budget.toml. It found on-target code that no budget counts:
> - kernel (baremetal): cell.rs 3 (documented), arch/riscv/smp.rs 3 (documented), arch/riscv/physmap.rs 1 (documented), debug/shell.rs 1 and debug/macros.rs 1. The debug/ uses have no SAFETY comment, and print! expands the macros.rs one at every call site. That contradicts the toml header's claim that "all unsafe in the kernel and loader now carries a SAFETY comment".
> - libs/abi (redoubt-abi, linked by kernel and loader): arch/riscv/{mod,process,syscall}.rs 11 uses, all undocumented. Shared modules (syscall.rs, stringbuffer.rs, carton.rs, messages/…) add about 40 more, mostly undocumented. This is the legacy xous ABI.
> - Excluded as not production: kernel/src/test.rs and arch/hosted (host-only), tests/programs, vendor/getrandom, bios/ (RustSBI, owner-controlled, unchanged).
> Per git -S, none of these kernel files was ever in a budget. T1c and IPC1 did not introduce this. The archive warned about it (§11: "cannot detect an entirely omitted component without a coverage inventory").
> 
> My recommendation: a small tooling follow-up before K5 takes the kernel, since after that K5 is the kernel's only writer:
> (1) add the five kernel files to their budget groups, with ceilings raised by exactly the counted uses and justified as coverage, not new unsafe;
> (2) add SAFETY comments to the two debug/ sites;
> (3) for libs/abi, either budget its on-target modules at honest counts now, or record them explicitly as K6 debt, since K6 deletes the legacy interface.
> Alternative: record the whole gap as deferred non-blocking debt and fold it into K6.
> I have not edited tests/unsafe-budget.toml or kernel code; neither is in my owned paths.
> 
> This decides whether T1c's criterion "normal ratchet runs enumerate the actual production sources" is met. I set the T1c row to merged, because its reviews are valid and it is integrated. Revert it to review if you count this gap as a T1c gate.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `df894b6d3b54758310160d7e7c3d1878` · 2026-09-24T05:35:30Z

> Good finding. Settled by WP-T1c's own criterion, not an owner decision: "normal ratchet runs enumerate the actual production sources and report honest counts. Do not raise budgets to hide newly uncovered debt; report any pre-existing overage separately." Uncounted on-target files mean the criterion is not met, so put the T1c row back to `review` until this lands.
> 
> Decision: close the gap now, inside G1, before K5 makes the kernel single-writer. Budget everything at honest counts, including libs/abi: counting is cheap, and deferring would leave production code unenumerated. Record libs/abi's undocumented uses as pre-existing debt (K6 deletes the legacy interface) rather than documenting all ~50 now. Details in your new assignment.
